blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
LLM agents are starting to own the full customer experience. Soon, LLMs may be
selling and buying on behalf of companies and customers respectively. Small
models are more cost-efficient at scale, but can reinforcement learning train
them into competent sellers? We train four Gemma 4 checkpoints (2.3B to 31B
effective parameters) with GRPO on a programmatic utility reward for bilateral
multi-issue bargaining, and evaluate every arm on the same 1,152
negotiations against two frontier buyers it never saw in training. With the
same learning rate ( 10 − 6 10^{-6} ) for every size, the gain of the RL model over its
base rises from + 0.001 +0.001 at 2.3B to + 0.078 +0.078 at 31B. Each
size was trained once and the two smallest checkpoints use a different
architecture, so we fit no scaling law. Tripling the learning rate, with the
same or fewer training steps, improves on the shared rate at every size by + 0.032 +0.032 (2.3B) to + 0.081 +0.081 (4.5B). In exploratory
comparisons with two frontier models run as sellers, the 12B seller trained at
the tripled rate scores above both, though its untrained base already scores as
high as they do. The 4.5B seller at that rate shows no detectable difference
from either and fits on one 48 GB GPU. A further 2.3B arm at
ten times the shared rate raises pooled score, but its gain concentrates on the
evaluation buyer that shares a model family with the training pool. These
results suggest tuning the learning rate before concluding that a small model
cannot learn to negotiate, and testing against buyers from more than one model
family.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Agents are beginning to act in workflows with direct economic consequences
(sales, procurement, marketplaces, contract negotiation), where negotiation
quality determines the value captured or conceded. Serving a frontier model for every recurring exchange
is costly and can conflict with latency, privacy and local-deployment
constraints, which favours small models specialized for agentic sub-tasks [ 6 ] . Negotiation tests that specialization on a sub-task
where a weak agent concedes real value.
Prompting alone has not made LLMs strong negotiators. They model counterparty
preferences accurately yet fail to convert them into compensated trades [ 11 ] , and only strong models improved from
self-play with in-context critique [ 14 ] . We therefore train
with a verifiable, outcome-aligned utility reward. In the closest prior work, Bergemann et al. [7] fine-tune Qwen3 8B and 14B with GRPO for bilateral
trade but run the sizes as independent tracks “with no cross-size comparisons”
and, with only two sizes, cannot “separate capacity from pretraining
differences”. We
ask whether RL improves each size over its base, how the gain varies with size,
and whether that pattern changes with the learning rate.

blocks.en: 2 Related work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Bilateral multi-issue bargaining is the canonical setting in which distributive
and integrative issues coexist, so skill means both claiming a fixed pie and
enlarging it by logrolling [ 34 , 29 , 3 ] . Recent benchmarks report surplus and diagnostic metrics
beyond deal rate, which conflates agreeableness with competence [ 39 , 8 ] . Xia et al. [37] report that larger models
are not necessarily better bargainers; they study base models and we study
the gain from RL. Our held-out buyer panel follows the cross-play evaluation
of Davidson et al. [12] and the leaderboard-overfitting result of Singh et al. [32] . Pre-LLM neural negotiators split a
dialogue-act strategy layer from generation [ 23 , 18 ] ; our seller learns strategy inside the language
policy, with no act layer and no dialogue supervision. DeepSeek-AI et al. [13] warn that large-scale RL on a small base “may not even achieve the performance
of distillation”; we test no distillation arm, and our 2.3B shared-rate
result is consistent with the warning. In adjacent settings, Liu et al. [24] train small models with zero-sum multi-turn self-play
where we use a fixed
external buyer pool; Haque et al. [17] study RL robustness for
small language-model agents.

blocks.en:
Liu et al. [25] train
a 30B MoE model with RLVR in a multi-buyer market and conclude that RL on verifiable
environments “is a more effective driver of utility than raw parameter scaling.”
That is a fixed-size comparison against larger untrained baselines. In our data,
RL improves on the base at 2.3B only once the learning rate is raised, and even
then the seller ( 0.460 0.460 ) scores below the untrained
12B base ( 0.525 0.525 ). Bergemann et al. [7] is single-issue and distributive
where ours is multi-issue; its RL stage recovers deal rate while eroding surplus,
and at 2.3B our shared-rate arm does the opposite. On scaling, Tan et al. [33] fit RL
post-training on single-turn mathematical reasoning across the dense Qwen2.5
series and find larger models consistently more compute- and data-efficient, with
a saturation trend in the fitted form [ 21 , 20 ] ; we know of no such study for a multi-agent task. In a learned-reward RLHF setting, Hou et al. [19] find that
“larger policy models benefit less
from RLHF with a fixed reward model.” Size and compute allocation are not
separable, since larger policies buy fewer rollouts per FLOP [ 36 ] .

We train with NeMo-RL’s GRPO-style estimator [ 31 , 27 ] (group-normalized advantages with a
leave-one-out baseline, no learned value model) on its multi-turn rollout

Opens with terms is the share of episodes in which the seller names at least one of the domain’s terms at turn 1, for the same-size base and then the arm. blocks.en:
Across four Gemma 4 checkpoints trained once each, the shared-LR gain point
estimates rise with size, and at the early checkpoints tripling the learning
rate improves on the shared rate at every size, with the largest point estimate

practical lessons: tune the learning rate before concluding that a small model
cannot learn to negotiate, and evaluate it against buyers from more than one
model family.

The protocol prespecifies four anti-Goodhart guards: deal rate must
not collapse while U ~ \tilde{U} rises, the bad-parse fraction must stay flat, mean turns
must not saturate at the cap, and five transcripts per RL’d arm per domain family
are read by hand. Welfare appears there as a secondary metric, not as a guard. The
other checks reported here (walk-aways, JSON leakage, template-tag leaks, unfilled
placeholders, the buyer-family split, opener concentration and held-out role
confusion) were added as successive evaluation rounds surfaced them and entered through the
deviation log rather than the frozen protocol. Opener concentration and held-out
role confusion in particular were recorded as guard failures for the 31B 3 × \times LR arm only after its readings were in hand; the 12B
3 × \times LR arm’s comparable
readings, evaluated earlier, had been logged as a property of the recipe. The split of the list into
“utility and format” guards, which the 31B 3 × \times LR arm passes, and “style”
guards, which it fails, was drawn the same way, after seeing this arm. Of the
guards fixed in advance, this arm passes all four. The two it fails, opener
concentration and held-out role confusion, are post-hoc style guards, and neither
measures what the seller extracts or whether the buyer can parse its turns.

blocks.en:
The four sizes ship different chat templates. The divergence is present in the
current published repositories of all four sizes, not an unsynced artefact, and
both variants render balanced turn tags. With thinking mode
disabled (the setting every arm runs) the conventional checkpoints’ template appends an empty
thought-channel prologue to the generation prompt that the E-series template does
not, so E-series generation prompts are 10 10 tokens against the conventional sizes’ 14 14 : E2B, E4B …<|turn>model\n 12B, 31B …<|turn>model\n<|channel>thought\n<channel|> We use each model’s own published template. Grafting the conventional template
onto the E-series would condition those models on a prefix pattern absent from
their own instruction tuning, which is a larger and less predictable intervention
than the difference it removes. Each
arm’s base counterpart is served with the same template as its trained
counterpart, so the base-versus-RL contrast, the quantity the paper reports,
is unaffected. Because the rollout driver tokenizes environment observations
raw, the environment must emit the buyer’s turn tags itself; we derive them per
arm from that arm’s tokenizer by differencing renders of a test dialogue, and
assert the extraction round-trips on a multi-turn history before training starts.
Every served prompt was verified by tokenizing and detokenizing it before the arm
was evaluated, and no arm produced a template-tag leak into buyer-visible text.

blocks.en:
None of the five 3 × \times and 10 × \times LR arms is in the frozen arm
matrix , which names one learning rate per size. Seeds, buyers, domains, sampling,
horizon and analysis follow the protocol exactly, so all five pair
scenario-for-scenario with every other arm.
blocks.zh:
5个3分相和10分相和相和相和相和相相相和的LR臂都没有放入被冻结的手臂中
矩阵,每个大小命名一个学习率。 种子、购买者、域、采样、
地平线与分析完全遵循协议 所以所有五对
假想与所有其他手臂。

blocks.en:
The 10 × \times LR Sonnet 5 cell did not clear the pre-run pilot
gate , returning 3 bad parses in 54 turns where the gate requires zero. We ran
it regardless, because that arm’s format stability is what it was
commissioned to measure and aborting would have discarded the finding.
blocks.zh:
10x\times LR Sonnet 5 单元格未清除预运行飞行员
在54个转弯中返回3个差分位置, 我们跑了
不管怎么说,因为那支手臂的形式稳定
被委托测量和中止 将会放弃这个发现。

blocks.en:
Two schedules per 104-step arm , as in
Appendix H , with 40 or 48 continued steps
depending on where the parent run stopped.

每104步臂有两个时间表,如:
附录H,有40或48个持续步骤

blocks.en:
Serving topology. The 31B arms are served with four
accelerators rather than two; at two the KV cache cannot hold the 16k context.
The serving argument string is otherwise identical across arms, and the 31B
base arm it is contrasted against is served the same way.
blocks.zh:
服务于地貌学. 31B武器装有4个
加速器而非两个;在两个 KV 缓存中不能持有 16k 上下文 。
现在的参数弦在其他方面是相同的, 和31B
反之则以同样方式使用。

blocks.en:
Nash distance and Pareto efficiency are not reported. We did not
compute them for this paper; joint welfare is the only efficiency proxy.
blocks.zh:
纳什距离和帕雷托效率没有报告. 我们没有
为本文计算它们;联合福利是唯一的效率代用.

blocks.en:
Strategy descriptors were added at camera-ready , in response to
review: Table 2 , its intervals in Table 9 ,
and the closing-turn shares in Section 5 . All are computed from
the frozen evaluation transcripts. The Δ \Delta columns use the same pairing and
seed-cluster bootstrap as every other contrast, restricted to the scenarios both
arms closed. None was prespecified, and all are exploratory.
blocks.zh:
为响应以下要求,在摄影机准备时增加了战略说明
审查:表2,表9中的间隔
以及第5节的收盘股票。 全部计算自
冻结的评价记录。 \\ Delta 列使用相同的配对和
种子组的靴子作为其他各种对比,仅限于两种情况
手臂关闭。 没有预先规定,而且都是探索性的。

blocks.en:
The buyer-split interval was added at camera-ready. The
10 × \times LR arm’s gain against each buyer and their difference
(Appendix E ) use the same pairing and bootstrap.
blocks.zh:
购买者- 分接间隔是相机准备后添加的。 这个
10 × Times LR arm 对每个买方的收益及其差额
(附录 E)使用同一种配对和靴子.

blocks.en:
Transient infrastructure failures produced error rows in several
runs. Every affected episode was re-run, and the results underlying this paper
contain zero error rows.

运行。 每集都重播 本文内容
包含零出错行。
